429:
- A cook, or something?
- It all depends on ability.
430:
I have an acquaintance, also a scientist,
only three grades of schooling,
431:
and he can draw a ten-ruble note in half an hour,
you can’t tell it from the real one!
432:
- Well, is it him?
- Hell knows... I’ll check.
433:
- Excuse me, do you have a match?
- I don’t smoke.
434:
- What? - No, not him.
- A cop. - Exactly.
435:
The check showed that at the addresses
of the Docent’s accomplices, the helmet isn’t there.
436:
The last version remains—cloakroom attendant
Prokhorov.
437:
However, we failed to check this version:
Prokhorov didn’t show up for the meeting.
438:
He likely suspected something. Quit his job,
didn’t show up at home.
440:
And to you—our deepest apologies, enormous thanks.
Take off the wig, wash off the tattoos,
441:
go home, celebrate New Year’s. Thank you very much.
- What about mine?
442: And your wards—we’ll return them to their place today.
443:
And if the cloakroom attendant turns up,
we might be needed again?
444:
I didn’t want to tell you, but today Bely—the Docent—
escaped from the colony.
445:
Unbelievable, but true. It’s dangerous for you to remain
in that appearance.
446:
Maybe tomorrow? It’s still New Year’s, and they
tried in their own way too.
447:
We live outside the city, it’s unlikely
the Docent can find us.
448:
All right, but don’t take a step off the dacha!
Yes, we forwarded your letter
449:
to Sheremetyev’s wife—here is her reply.
Addressed to him.
450:
- You’ll have lunch with us on the first—you promise?
- We promise!
451:
Pity—such a good woman, and her father’s
a fence, a speculator.
452:
Why are you yelling? Who allowed you to come out?
- He’s come... A bad person.
454:
The New Year has come. I wish that in this
new year everything will be new for you.
455:
Anything can happen, but know this:
wherever you are, wherever I am,
456:
I will always remember you,
and I will definitely find you.
457:
- And now... one minute...
- Where’d he go?
458:
Who knows? You can’t make anything out
of him now.
459:
What’s there to make out? Wherever you are, he says,
he’ll find you and cut your throat.
461:
They say he slit Ryaby’s throat with a razor—snip, and goodbye.
- He’s gone completely rabid, the jackal.
462:
Who has come to you? Santa Claus has come to you,
he brought you gifts!
463:
- Fedya, come here. - What did I do?
- Come, come. Wear them in good health—house slippers.
464:
- What the hell do I need them for? I don’t even have a home.
- You will—everything’s ahead.
465:
- For now, they’ll come in handy in prison too. Wear them.
- All you do is croak.
466:
This is for you, Vasya... Gavrila Petrovich, this is for you.
- Thank you.
467:
- Pure wool.
- This is for you too.
470:
- Do you have to get drunk like a pig?
- What else is there to do?
471:
We can just sit and talk
heart to heart.
472:
I’m not a prosecutor to have heart-to-heart talks with you.
- We can play something.
473:
Look at him! Found a sucker to play with you!
You’ve got nine aces in your deck.
474: Why does it have to be cards?
475:
Here’s a good game—cities.
I say “Moscow,”
476:
and you, on the last letter “A”—Astrakhan.
And you, on “N”—Novgorod, get it?
477: Now you, Fedya—say one that starts with “D.”
478:
Vorkuta.
Why? I served time there.
479:
- All right. And you, then, on “A.”
- Dzhambul. - What does Dzhambul have to do with it?
480:
Because it’s warm there, that’s my home,
that’s my mom.
481:
Then let’s play like this. I’ll go out, you
hide something, I’ll come back—I’ll find it.
482:
- You’d better find our helmet.
- Be quiet.
483:
- We’ll hide it and he’ll “watch the hole”?
- Why? You go out and hide it.
484:
And you watch so I don’t peek.
And why me? Anything happens—right away it’s Fedya.
485:
- And I’ll tear your mouth open, you filthy little bastard!
- Mouth, mouth...
486:
- Docent, were you ever little?
- I was.
487:
- You had a dad, a mom?
- I did.
488: Why are you so angry? Why like a dog?
490:
- Came on his own.
- Ah, you’re here too.
491:
I was going to come to you, but I can feel it—
there’s an ambush there.
492: Mityai, I need to lie low.
494:
- Where are we going?
- Come on.
495:
- Sorry, doctor, for bothering you for nothing.
- It’s fine.
496:
Give him some valerian, warm tea, and let him sleep.
- Thank you.
497:
- Does it hurt, Garik?
- It hurts, Vasya. Read.
499:
“Hello, dear Dad! We found out that
you’re in prison
500:
and we were very happy, because we thought
you were dead.”
501: What bastard told that little punk about Hmyr?
502:
“And Mom was happy too, because
when the letter came, she cried
503:
all day, and before that she said you were
a test pilot.”
505:
“And I’m still glad you’re alive, because
Mom says
507:
Exactly! Weak-willed—stole the common money
and blamed the cab driver.
508: Make tracks from here! I’ll knock your horns off, radish!
510:
Aren’t you ashamed! You’re 40 years old,
half your life is already gone.
511:
What’s behind you? What’s in the present?
What’s ahead?
512:
Darkness, filth, and nothing human!
Come to your senses while it’s not too late. That’s my advice.
513:
Listen, Docent, we’ve got to clear out:
the lady doctor will squeal to the police.
514:
- She won’t squeal. - Why not?
- I did her in—razor to the throat...
515: she’s in the well, you can go look.
516: How much did I have? One year.
518:
How much for the kindergarten and the apartment?
Let’s say ten!
520:
And for a lousy 14 years I’m supposed to put up with
that viper?
521:
The one the old woman put in the well?
Do what you want, I’m going to the police.
523:
And you? You’ll keep putting up with him
till death, yeah?
524: Vasya, I told him earlier: I’ve got a runny nose, and he...
525:
Enough, I’m sick of your runny nose.
Come here...
526:
- Where are you here?
- Right here.
527:
- What are you up to?
- We’re going to beat a carpet.
528:
All right, comrades. Finita la commedia.
First of all, I’m taking this off.
530:
I’ll serve my term and that’s it. I’ll quit!
Get a job.
531:
- As what? A watchman back at your collective farm.
- Why a watchman?
532:
I can shovel snow, lay bricks, or
be a translator—I know English.
533:
If only we’d brought the hat too!
Who’s the Docent? A crook.
534:
- There are lots of crooks, but only one hat.
- If we turned in the helmet, they’d cut our time.
535: Where did he put it? We checked everywhere.
536:
Crook! Did I tell you I have a runny nose?
And you: mouth, mouth.
537:
- Made me dive in that freezing cold!
- When did he make you dive?
538:
When we got nabbed. Remember? He says,
“I’m fishing,” and you dive.
539:
- Wait, what did he say about the fish then?
- “I’m fishing in an ice hole,
540:
- and you, Cross-Eyed, can you swim?”
- He hid the helmet in the ice hole—that’s what!
541:
Exactly! I remember, bad person!
In the ice hole, in Malakhovka!
542:
Why didn’t you say so? You lout! You could’ve left a note when you hanged yourself.
- Let’s go.
543:
- What about him?
- Nothing—let them pick him up themselves. Carrying a hog like that. Let’s go!
545:
- There’s nothing there.
- It’s there, on the bottom. We need to dive.
546:
Why me? Anything happens—right away Cross-Eyed.
Vasya, tell him to go in himself.
547: I can’t! It’s cold, I’ll get sick.
548:
- Just now he was hanging himself, now he’s afraid of catching a cold!
- Fitness greetings!
550:
- Where’s the boat station?
- Over there.
551: I’d sew you up, but I don’t have time to mess around!
552:
Now it makes two.
And there’s another one at the dacha.
554:
- One!
- Well done, Fyodor Petrovich, well done!
555:
- Two.
- The more we hand in, the better.
